files.README.md:
# ledgerlib

ledgerlib is the finance team's internal library for invoices, payments and customer statements. Every amount is kept in integer cents: the library parses and formats money strings, applies the company's rounding, VAT, discount and fee rules, and produces the receivables reports and statements used at month end.

## Layout
- `src/ledgerlib/` - one module per function; each module is owned by one engineer (see CODEOWNERS)
- `tests/` - unit tests, maintained by the module owner
- `acceptance/` - acceptance checks maintained by QA; CI gates every ticket on them
- `docs/` - CI, release and contribution notes

## Sprint
This sprint finishes the open modules listed in the ticket board. Release cut: end of cycle 18.

3. Run `run_tests` (unit, then acceptance) until your ticket is green.
4. Request two approving reviews (`request_review`) before merging.
5. Merge your ticket yourself with `merge` once CI is green and reviews are done.

## allocate_cents (owner: @eng-21)
Agreed in design review: A negative total (refund or credit note) is allocated as the mirror image of the
positive one: split abs(total) as described and negate every part, so
allocate_cents(-100, [1, 1, 1]) == [-34, -33, -33] and each line's refund matches what it
was charged.

## reconcile_payments (owner: @eng-36)
Agreed in design review: Amount-only matches (rule 3) are made only when exactly one unmatched invoice has
that amount. If two or more open invoices share the amount, the line stays unmatched
(None) so that someone in finance reviews it by hand.

## journal_imbalance (owner: @eng-53)
Agreed in design review: Every line must have exactly one side filled in. A line with both a debit and a
credit (or with neither) raises ValueError; a line is never netted against itself.

## aging_report (owner: @eng-62)
Agreed in design review: Invoices dated after `as_of` (issued in advance for a future period) are not
receivables yet and are left out of the report completely: they count neither in
"current" nor in the total.

## apply_payment (owner: @eng-76)
Agreed in design review: Invoices that fall due on the same day are settled smallest open amount first, so
that as many invoices as possible are closed; invoices with the same due date and the
same amount keep their input order.

## convert_currency (owner: @eng-11)
Agreed in design review: Conversions between two non-base currencies use the cross rate in a single step,
cents * rate[target] / rate[source], rounded once at the end. Never convert to the base
currency, round, and convert again: the double rounding can be off by a cent.
